```{r}
# ============================================================
# DataCo: Checkout-time profit prediction
# Multiple linear regression, Lasso, random forest, boosting
# ============================================================

# Run once if needed:
# install.packages(c("glmnet", "ranger", "gbm"))

library(glmnet)
library(ranger)
library(gbm)

set.seed(448)

input <- "D:/DataCo_cleaned.csv"
out <- "model_results"

dir.create(out, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

save_csv <- function(x, name) {
  write.csv(x, file.path(out, name), row.names = FALSE)
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Import data and select checkout-time predictors
# ------------------------------------------------------------

raw <- read.csv(
  input,
  check.names = FALSE,
  fileEncoding = "latin1"
)

# Standardize names, including names exported with dots.
names(raw) <- tolower(gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", names(raw)))
names(raw) <- gsub("^_|_$", "", names(raw))

predictors <- c(
  "order_item_quantity",
  "order_item_product_price",
  "order_item_discount_rate",
  "category_name",
  "customer_segment",
  "market",
  "order_region"
)

needed <- c("order_id", "benefit_per_order", predictors)

stopifnot(all(needed %in% names(raw)))

# Remove only exact full-record duplicates.
raw <- unique(raw)

d <- raw[, needed]
names(d)[1:2] <- c("order_id", "y")

num <- predictors[1:3]
catvars <- predictors[4:7]

stopifnot(
  all(vapply(d[, c("y", num)], is.numeric, logical(1)))
)

d <- d[is.finite(d$y) & !is.na(d$order_id), ]

for (v in catvars) {
  d[[v]] <- as.character(d[[v]])
}

# The whitelist excludes:
# Order Profit Per Order: duplicates the response.
# Order Item Profit Ratio: derived from profit.
# Delivery Status, actual shipping days, shipping date,
# Late_delivery_risk and Order Status: later information.
# Identifiers and personal information are not predictors.

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Split whole orders: 75% training, 25% testing
# ------------------------------------------------------------

ids <- unique(d$order_id)
train_ids <- sample(ids, floor(0.75 * length(ids)))

train <- d[d$order_id %in% train_ids, ]
test <- d[!d$order_id %in% train_ids, ]

stopifnot(!any(train$order_id %in% test$order_id))

# Assign each training order to one of five validation folds.
fold_map <- setNames(
  sample(rep(1:5, length.out = length(train_ids))),
  as.character(train_ids)
)

fold_id <- unname(fold_map[as.character(train$order_id)])

save_csv(
  data.frame(
    set = c("train", "test"),
    rows = c(nrow(train), nrow(test)),
    orders = c(length(train_ids), length(ids) - length(train_ids))
  ),
  "split_counts.csv"
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Preprocessing learned within each training fold
# ------------------------------------------------------------

learn_prep <- function(a) {

  med <- sapply(
    a[, num, drop = FALSE],
    function(z) median(z[is.finite(z)])
  )

  lev <- lapply(
    a[, catvars, drop = FALSE],
    function(z) sort(unique(z[!is.na(z) & nzchar(z)]))
  )

  modes <- sapply(a[, catvars, drop = FALSE], function(z) {
    z <- z[!is.na(z) & nzchar(z)]
    names(sort(table(z), decreasing = TRUE))[1]
  })

  stopifnot(all(is.finite(med)), all(lengths(lev) >= 2))

  list(med = med, lev = lev, modes = modes)
}

apply_prep <- function(a, p) {

  x <- a[, predictors, drop = FALSE]

  for (v in num) {
    x[[v]][!is.finite(x[[v]])] <- p$med[[v]]
  }

  for (v in catvars) {
    z <- x[[v]]
    z[is.na(z) | !z %in% p$lev[[v]]] <- p$modes[[v]]
    x[[v]] <- factor(z, levels = p$lev[[v]])
  }

  x
}

design <- function(x) model.matrix(~ ., x)

score <- function(y, pred) {
  c(
    RMSE = sqrt(mean((y - pred)^2)),
    MAE = mean(abs(y - pred)),
    R2 = 1 - sum((y - pred)^2) / sum((y - mean(y))^2)
  )
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Define tuning grids before test evaluation
# ------------------------------------------------------------

lambda <- 10^seq(2, -3, length.out = 30)

rf_grid <- expand.grid(
  mtry = c(2L, 7L),
  min_node = c(50L, 200L)
)

gb_grid <- expand.grid(
  depth = c(1L, 3L),
  rate = c(0.03, 0.10)
)

tree_grid <- c(100L, 300L, 600L)

cv <- data.frame()

record <- function(model, config, fold, y, pred) {

  s <- score(y, pred)

  cv <<- rbind(
    cv,
    data.frame(
      model, config, fold,
      RMSE = s[1],
      MAE = s[2],
      R2 = s[3],
      row.names = NULL
    )
  )
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Five-fold cross-validation grouped by order
# ------------------------------------------------------------

for (k in 1:5) {

  cat("CV fold", k, "of 5\n")

  a <- train[fold_id != k, ]
  b <- train[fold_id == k, ]

  pp <- learn_prep(a)

  xa <- apply_prep(a, pp)
  xb <- apply_prep(b, pp)

  ma <- design(xa)
  mb <- design(xb)

  # Multiple linear regression
  ols <- lm.fit(ma, a$y)

  beta <- ols$coefficients
  beta[is.na(beta)] <- 0

  # QR fitting handles redundant market/region indicators.
  record("Linear", 1, k, b$y, drop(mb %*% beta))

  # Lasso: fit a complete penalty path.
  lasso <- glmnet(
    ma[, -1],
    a$y,
    alpha = 1,
    lambda = lambda,
    standardize = TRUE
  )

  lp <- predict(lasso, newx = mb[, -1], s = lambda)

  for (j in seq_along(lambda)) {
    record("Lasso", j, k, b$y, lp[, j])
  }

  # Random forest
  for (j in seq_len(nrow(rf_grid))) {

    set.seed(448 + 100 * k + j)

    rf <- ranger(
      x = xa,
      y = a$y,
      num.trees = 300,
      mtry = rf_grid$mtry[j],
      min.node.size = rf_grid$min_node[j],
      respect.unordered.factors = "order",
      num.threads = 2
    )

    record(
      "Random forest", j, k, b$y,
      predict(rf, xb)$predictions
    )

    rm(rf)
  }

  # Gradient boosting
  for (j in seq_len(nrow(gb_grid))) {

    set.seed(1448 + 100 * k + j)

    gb <- gbm(
      y ~ .,
      data = data.frame(y = a$y, xa),
      distribution = "gaussian",
      n.trees = max(tree_grid),
      interaction.depth = gb_grid$depth[j],
      shrinkage = gb_grid$rate[j],
      n.minobsinnode = 50,
      bag.fraction = 0.8,
      verbose = FALSE,
      keep.data = FALSE,
      n.cores = 1
    )

    for (t in seq_along(tree_grid)) {

      key <- (j - 1L) * length(tree_grid) + t

      record(
        "Boosting", key, k, b$y,
        predict(gb, xb, n.trees = tree_grid[t])
      )
    }
  }

  gc()
}

save_csv(cv, "cv_fold_scores.csv")

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Select configurations using CV RMSE
# ------------------------------------------------------------

cv_mean <- aggregate(
  cbind(RMSE, MAE, R2) ~ model + config,
  cv,
  mean
)

cv_se <- aggregate(
  RMSE ~ model + config,
  cv,
  function(z) sd(z) / sqrt(length(z))
)

names(cv_se)[3] <- "RMSE_SE"

cv_mean <- merge(cv_mean, cv_se, by = c("model", "config"))

best <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(split(cv_mean, cv_mean$model), function(z) {
    z[which.min(z$RMSE), ]
  })
)

best <- best[order(best$RMSE), ]
rownames(best) <- NULL

save_csv(cv_mean, "cv_all_configurations.csv")
save_csv(best, "cv_best_models.csv")

# Freeze the preferred method before inspecting test results.
winner <- best$model[1]

ix <- setNames(best$config, best$model)

best_lambda <- lambda[ix[["Lasso"]]]
best_rf <- rf_grid[ix[["Random forest"]], ]

gkey <- ix[["Boosting"]]
gj <- (gkey - 1L) %/% length(tree_grid) + 1L
nt <- tree_grid[(gkey - 1L) %% length(tree_grid) + 1L]

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Refit selected configurations on all training orders
# ------------------------------------------------------------

pp <- learn_prep(train)

xt <- apply_prep(train, pp)
xe <- apply_prep(test, pp)

mt <- design(xt)
me <- design(xe)

ols <- lm.fit(mt, train$y)

beta <- ols$coefficients
beta[is.na(beta)] <- 0

lasso <- glmnet(
  mt[, -1],
  train$y,
  alpha = 1,
  lambda = lambda,
  standardize = TRUE
)

set.seed(448)

rf <- ranger(
  x = xt,
  y = train$y,
  num.trees = 300,
  mtry = best_rf$mtry,
  min.node.size = best_rf$min_node,
  respect.unordered.factors = "order",
  importance = "permutation",
  num.threads = 2
)

set.seed(448)

gb <- gbm(
  y ~ .,
  data = data.frame(y = train$y, xt),
  distribution = "gaussian",
  n.trees = nt,
  interaction.depth = gb_grid$depth[gj],
  shrinkage = gb_grid$rate[gj],
  n.minobsinnode = 50,
  bag.fraction = 0.8,
  verbose = FALSE,
  keep.data = FALSE
)

predict_model <- function(model, x) {

  m <- design(x)

  switch(
    model,
    "Linear" = drop(m %*% beta),
    "Lasso" = drop(predict(lasso, m[, -1], s = best_lambda)),
    "Random forest" = predict(rf, x)$predictions,
    "Boosting" = predict(gb, x, n.trees = nt)
  )
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Held-out test performance and simple benchmarks
# ------------------------------------------------------------

preds <- data.frame(
  order_id = test$order_id,
  actual = test$y,
  Mean_baseline = mean(train$y),
  Median_baseline = median(train$y)
)

for (model in best$model) {
  preds[[model]] <- predict_model(model, xe)
}

test_scores <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(names(preds)[-(1:2)], function(nm) {
    data.frame(
      model = nm,
      t(score(test$y, preds[[nm]])),
      row.names = NULL
    )
  })
)

save_csv(test_scores, "test_scores.csv")
save_csv(preds, "test_predictions.csv")

# Secondary evaluation: sum predictions within each order.
# This assumes the recorded row profits are additive.
op <- aggregate(
  preds[, -1],
  list(order_id = preds$order_id),
  sum
)

order_scores <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(names(op)[-(1:2)], function(nm) {
    data.frame(
      model = nm,
      t(score(op$actual, op[[nm]])),
      row.names = NULL
    )
  })
)

save_csv(order_scores, "order_sum_test_scores.csv")

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 9. Coefficients and feature importance
# ------------------------------------------------------------

save_csv(
  data.frame(
    term = names(ols$coefficients),
    estimate = ols$coefficients
  ),
  "linear_coefficients.csv"
)

lc <- as.matrix(coef(lasso, s = best_lambda))

save_csv(
  data.frame(term = rownames(lc), estimate = lc[, 1]),
  "lasso_coefficients.csv"
)

save_csv(
  data.frame(
    feature = names(rf$variable.importance),
    importance = rf$variable.importance
  ),
  "rf_oob_importance.csv"
)

save_csv(
  summary(gb, plotit = FALSE),
  "boosting_relative_influence.csv"
)

# Test permutation importance for the already-selected model.
# These results are for interpretation, not further tuning.
set.seed(1448)

base_rmse <- score(test$y, preds[[winner]])[1]

pi <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(predictors, function(v) {

    inc <- replicate(3, {
      xp <- xe
      xp[[v]] <- sample(xp[[v]])

      score(test$y, predict_model(winner, xp))[1] - base_rmse
    })

    data.frame(
      feature = v,
      RMSE_increase = mean(inc),
      shuffle_sd = sd(inc)
    )
  })
)

save_csv(
  pi[order(-pi$RMSE_increase), ],
  "winner_permutation_importance.csv"
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 10. Paired bootstrap comparison with linear regression
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Resample whole orders to preserve dependence among their rows.
set.seed(2448)

e <- data.frame(
  order_id = test$order_id,
  winner = (test$y - preds[[winner]])^2,
  linear = (test$y - preds[["Linear"]])^2,
  n = 1
)

ag <- aggregate(e[, -1], list(order_id = e$order_id), sum)

delta <- replicate(500, {

  z <- ag[sample.int(nrow(ag), replace = TRUE), ]

  sqrt(sum(z$winner) / sum(z$n)) -
    sqrt(sum(z$linear) / sum(z$n))
})

save_csv(
  data.frame(
    comparison = paste(winner, "minus Linear RMSE"),
    difference = base_rmse -
      score(test$y, preds[["Linear"]])[1],
    lower = quantile(delta, 0.025),
    upper = quantile(delta, 0.975)
  ),
  "paired_order_bootstrap.csv"
)

capture.output(
  list(
    selected_model = winner,
    lambda = best_lambda,
    random_forest = best_rf,
    boosting = cbind(gb_grid[gj, ], trees = nt)
  ),
  file = file.path(out, "selected_parameters.txt")
)

capture.output(
  sessionInfo(),
  file = file.path(out, "session_info.txt")
)

print(best)
print(test_scores)

# Interpret Lasso coefficients:
lasso_coefficients <- data.frame(
  term = rownames(lc),
  estimate = lc[, 1]
)

print(
  lasso_coefficients[lasso_coefficients$estimate != 0, ]
)

print(pi[order(-pi$RMSE_increase), ])
```
